answer: An opal is accepted only when its rim is a cast of one knoll, taken in the garden bed beneath that rise. The garden seats the rim on the outline of the knoll, and a copied sentence has no rim to seat. The rim is one closed curve. Breaking it so two keys can each hold a piece leaves both pieces short of the outline, and neither piece seats. A rim pressed outside the garden does not meet the knoll, so the opal stays loose.
